scenarios.name: SMB SaaS — Fast Close

customer_requested_changes.change: Net 45 instead of Net 30
60-day notice instead of 90-day notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees
No change — customer accepts 99.5%

scenarios.context: Startup on a tight budget. Decision-maker is the CFO who has approved the deal but wants minor commercial tweaks. Sales rep has authority to close without legal review if total risk is low. Customer is not in a regulated industry.
scenarios.sales_priority: Speed — deal needs to close this month for Q1 revenue recognition

pre_approved_concessions: Net 45 payment terms for deals under EUR 50K
Remove auto-renewal with explicit renewal clause instead

scenarios.name: Mid-Market — Regulated Industry

deal.product: SaaS Platform — Professional Tier + Implementation Services

customer_requested_changes.change: 99.9% availability — platform is used for batch release documentation
60-day notice, approval (not just objection) required for each subprocessor
24 hours notification — regulatory requirement under MDR
24-month fee cap instead of 12-month — customer processes safety-critical documentation
Customer requires right to audit TechForward's information security controls annually, or upon a security incident, at Customer's cost with 30 days' notice

scenarios.context: Medical device company subject to EU MDR regulation. Their use of the platform involves documentation required by law to be accurate and available. A platform outage during a batch release could cause a regulatory violation. Customer's legal team has involvement. Austrian law preferred but German law acceptable.
scenarios.sales_priority: Compliance confidence — customer needs to justify the purchase to their quality manager
scenarios.legal_review_reason: Regulated industry, elevated liability ask, audit rights request

regulated_industry_special_terms: 99.9% SLA is available as an add-on (EUR 8,000/year uplift — confirm pricing with sales ops)
24-hour breach notification is operationally feasible — pre-approved
Audit rights are accepted with: max 1 per year, 30-day notice, scope limited to information security controls, TechForward may propose alternative assurance (SOC 2 report) in lieu

scenarios.name: Enterprise — Full Negotiation

deal.product: SaaS Platform — Enterprise Tier + Managed Services + Custom Integrations

scenarios.customer_requested_changes: See customer-redlines-enterprise-deal.md for full redline set
scenarios.context: This is TechForward's largest deal this year. Customer is a publicly listed manufacturing company with a sophisticated legal and procurement team. Deal involves custom integrations into their SAP environment. Platform will be used for real-time production scheduling — any outage has direct operational impact. Legal review is mandatory. CFO sign-off required for any liability cap above EUR 720K.
scenarios.sales_priority: Deal is strategic — acceptable to spend 2–3 weeks negotiating. Revenue impact of delay: EUR 40K/month.
scenarios.legal_review_reason: Enterprise deal above EUR 500K, complex redlines including liability, IP escrow, MFC clause

requires_cfo_approval: Liability cap above 24 months of fees
Refund of prepaid fees on convenience termination
deal_breakers: Most Favored Customer clause — TechForward does not offer MFC commitments
Liability cap above 36 months of fees

scenarios.name: Public Sector — Government Procurement

deal.product: SaaS Platform — Enterprise Tier (on-premise hybrid deployment)

customer_requested_changes.change: Customer insists on using EVB-IT SaaS standard terms rather than TechForward's standard contract
Data must reside exclusively on servers in Germany (data sovereignty requirement) — no cloud subprocessors outside Germany
German administrative courts have jurisdiction — not commercial courts
Price is fixed for the entire 3-year contract term — no adjustments permitted under public procurement rules
TechForward and all subprocessors must hold BSI IT-Grundschutz certification or equivalent within 12 months of contract signing

scenarios.context: Federal agency with strict data sovereignty, security certification, and procurement law requirements. Procurement is governed by German public procurement law (GWB/VgV). Contract must follow EVB-IT terms which differ significantly from TechForward's standard. Legal and public sector specialist review is mandatory. TechForward's product team must confirm German-only hosting is technically feasible.
scenarios.sales_priority: Strategic — government reference customer. Revenue is secondary to partnership value.
scenarios.legal_review_reason: Public sector contract — entirely different legal framework (EVB-IT), data sovereignty requirements, BSI certification

requires_specialist_review: Product / infrastructure team for Germany-only hosting feasibility
deal_breakers: EVB-IT terms must be evaluated — TechForward has not previously contracted on EVB-IT
BSI IT-Grundschutz certification timeline may not be achievable within 12 months

scenarios.name: US-Based Customer — Cross-Border Deal

customer.name: NovaTech Inc.
customer.jurisdiction: United States (Delaware incorporation, operations in NY and CA)

customer_requested_changes.change: New York law instead of German law
JAMS arbitration in New York instead of Berlin courts
Net 45 in USD (request to convert deal to USD denomination)
Replace GDPR-focused DPA with a US-centric privacy addendum covering CCPA/CPRA only — customer believes GDPR does not apply as they are a US entity
Cap limited to fees paid in last 6 months — 'industry standard for SaaS' per customer's legal team
Customer accepts TechForward's standard language

scenarios.context: US customer that processes data of EU-based end users through TechForward's platform, making GDPR applicable to TechForward as the processor regardless of where NovaTech is incorporated. Customer's legal team is unfamiliar with GDPR. Governing law and jurisdiction need careful handling — some compromise may be possible but German mandatory law provisions cannot be waived.
scenarios.sales_priority: Close before quarter end — customer has budget expiry on June 1.
scenarios.legal_review_reason: Cross-border deal, governing law compromise required, GDPR applicability dispute, currency change requires finance approval

pre_approved: Net 45 payment terms for enterprise deals
New York law as an alternative governing law (with German mandatory law carve-out) — pre-approved for US customers
requires_legal_review: GDPR applicability determination — DPO must confirm EU data subject involvement
JAMS arbitration — acceptable in principle but seat should remain in EU if possible
6-month liability cap — below minimum acceptable (12 months)
deal_breakers: Replacing GDPR DPA with CCPA-only addendum if EU personal data is processed — non-negotiable

scenarios.name: Renewal + Upsell — Existing Customer

deal.product: SaaS Platform — Professional Tier (upgrade from Basic) + AI Analytics Module

customer_requested_changes.change: Price freeze for 3 years — no increases allowed (customer cites 50% price increase from Basic to Professional as justification)
Remove auto-renewal — replace with explicit renewal process
99.9% — customer experienced 3 outages in prior contract that affected operations
Customer requests retroactive service credit of EUR 8,500 for 3 outages in the prior contract period before signing the renewal

scenarios.context: Longstanding customer with good payment history. Upgrading to a more expensive tier and extending to 3 years. Customer had genuine service disruptions in the prior term. Retaining this customer is important for ARR targets. Sales rep has asked whether the retroactive credit can be offered as a goodwill gesture as part of the renewal package.
scenarios.sales_priority: Retention — losing this customer to a competitor would reduce ARR by EUR 108K.

pre_approved: Remove auto-renewal with explicit renewal clause — pre-approved
Price freeze for term (no annual increases) for renewals above EUR 100K/year — pre-approved with VP Sales approval
99.9% SLA is available as an add-on — confirm uplift pricing with sales ops
Goodwill service credit up to EUR 10,000 for prior documented outages — requires VP Customer Success approval

pre_approved_concessions: Reduce late payment interest from 1.5% to 1% per month
Extend invoice dispute window from 21 to 30 days
Remove auto-renewal (replace with explicit renewal clause)
Reduce convenience termination notice from 90 to 60 days (fees remain non-refundable)
Extend data export period from 45 to 90 days

additional_concessions: Price freeze for contract term on renewals
99.9% SLA (with uplift pricing confirmation from sales ops)
Arbitration as alternative to Berlin courts (seat in EU)

mandatory_triggers: Customer proposes their own contract template instead of TechForward's
Liability cap below 12 months or above 24 months of fees
Any carve-out from the liability cap exclusions
IP ownership changes or source code escrow requests
Regulated industry with compliance-specific requirements (MDR, financial services, defense)
Cross-border deal with non-EU governing law

absolute_deal_breakers: Most Favored Customer (MFC) pricing clause — TechForward policy does not permit MFC commitments
Liability cap below 6 months of fees
Waiving GDPR DPA obligations where EU personal data is processed
Customer ownership of TechForward's Background IP or core platform
Perpetual, irrevocable right to use TechForward IP post-termination without ongoing payment
Liquidated damages clauses above 2x annual contract value
Mandatory compliance with EVB-IT or other government procurement terms without legal specialist review
